headline: Fed rate hike pushed to December, lifting equities to fresh records
tldr: S&P 500 near record highs and STOXX 600 at fourth consecutive record close after weak US jobs print delays Fed hike to December.
ASML up 2.15% and defence stocks gaining; AMD down 1.21% on profit-taking; Hormuz news remains the key oil risk to watch.
FPL deadline confirmed at 17:30 Friday 21 Aug; Timber a coin flip, Garner and Saliba confirmed avoids for GW1.
UK motor insurance forecast loss-making through 2027 with combined ratio of 108%; John Lewis now an active panel manager across 1.4 million customers.
UK data roles average £77,800 in 2026; 42% of data teams report into CTO, not a Head of Data — shape leadership pitches accordingly.

sections.title: Markets
sections.body:
Today is Monday 8 August, so markets are opening fresh after Friday's close. Here's what the data shows — Friday's closes are the latest confirmed figures, and today's early moves are captured in the pre-fetched portfolio data.

---

**Markets — Monday 8 August 2026**

The dominant carry-over from Friday is the Fed rate-path repricing. 
The weak US jobs print drove stocks higher while bond yields fell, with the S&P 500 rising towards a record and on course for its best week since April.
 
Money markets still project a Fed hike in 2026, but not before December
 — that pushback in the hiking timeline is what's continuing to support equities into Monday's open.

In Europe, Friday was a strong session. 
The pan-European STOXX 600 rallied to its fourth consecutive record close on Friday, with Germany's DAX, France's CAC 40, and the FTSE 100 all securing gains.
 
The FTSE 100 gained 42 points (+0.39%) to close at 10,910.
 
Investors stayed cautious over a lasting Strait of Hormuz deal; precious metals miners outperformed, with Fresnillo and Endeavour up 5.3% and 4.1% respectively.
 
Shell and BP fell as oil remained lower on the week.


In Asia on Friday, 
the Nikkei shed 0.12% to 65,607, extending tech losses for a second session on AI trade concerns, with sentiment also weighed by a rebound in oil and weak domestic data — Japanese household spending fell 3.3% in June, well below the 1% increase expected.


This morning's portfolio moves are modest and consistent with the broader tone: risk-on but selective. ASML +2.15% is the standout — semiconductor capital equipment benefiting from the tech-friendly rate narrative. AMD is the outlier at -1.21%, suggesting some post-earnings profit-taking after its strong run earlier in the week. BAE Systems +0.91% and QinetiQ +1.19% continue to tick higher on defence spending tailwinds. The Nikkei-linked IJPN +0.78% is slightly outperforming the broader VUSA/VEVE, possibly recovering from Friday's AI-driven dip.

**Watch today:** any further Hormuz news will move oil and therefore inflation expectations — the chain running from oil → core PCE → Fed → equities remains live.

sections.body:
**Deadline: Friday 21 Aug, 17:30 BST** *(note: corrected from yesterday — the pre-fetched data confirms 17:30, not 18:30)*

**Prices**


Prices remain locked until the GW1 deadline; movement only begins after Friday's cut-off.
 Nothing to chase in the market right now — squad construction is the only lever available.

**Injuries & doubts — what's new**

The flagged list has a couple of developments worth noting beyond yesterday's summary:

- **J. Timber (Arsenal, £6.5m)** — groin injury, expected back 21 Aug. That's the same day as the deadline; treat as a coin flip until the pre-match presser.
- **Garner (Everton)** — expected back 22 Aug, which is *after* the deadline. Confirmed avoid.
- **Burstow (Hull City)** — has joined Sheffield Wednesday on loan for the season; remove from any draft consideration entirely.
- 
Saliba also features on the confirmed avoids list
 — worth noting if you're building an Arsenal defensive stack.
- 
Šeško, Martínez and Tielemans (all Man Utd) can still become available, but none should be treated as a guaranteed GW1 starter yet.


**Differentials being discussed**

- 
Vuskovic (Brighton) is appearing in differential drafts — the new signing scored 6 goals and 2 assists in the Bundesliga last season.

- 
Value midfielders at £6.0–6.5m with nailed minutes — Anderson and Amad are among the names circulating
 as low-ownership options to separate from the template.
- 
There is hype around Man Utd's opener, making Senne Lammens (GK) a popular differential candidate after impressing last season.

sections.title: Data & BI
sections.body:
The July Power BI story was already covered in yesterday's briefing. The BigQuery continuous queries GA and Graph preview were also covered. The semantic layer/AI/MetricFlow angle was covered too. Let me check what's genuinely new — the search results surface a few things not in yesterday's briefing:

1. **PBIR (Power BI Enhanced Report Format) being enabled by default in July/August** — this is a meaningful structural change not covered yesterday
2. **Power BI Desktop Bridge** — agents/external tools connecting to a running Desktop session, not covered yesterday
3. **Downloading from semantic model now gives empty report** — a behaviour change
4. **Snowflake Semantic View Autopilot** — ML-based metric discovery, not covered yesterday
5. **dbt State of Analytics Engineering 2026** — trust rose from 66% to 83% as top priority
6. **Looker self-service Explores** — bring your own data to Looker's semantic layer

These are genuinely new. Let me write the section around what's fresh.

---

**Data & BI** · 8 August 2026

**Power BI — two structural changes to watch this month**

The July feature summary was covered yesterday. Two items from it deserve separate attention now they're actively rolling out:

- **PBIR on by default.** 
Microsoft planned to enable PBIR by default in Power BI Desktop in July/August, contingent on a clean service rollout, with General Availability for PBIR and PBIP to follow assuming the rollout progresses smoothly through the summer.
 If your team uses Git-based deployment pipelines, test now — PBIR changes the on-disk report format and can break assumptions in existing CI/CD scripts.

- **Desktop Bridge in preview.** 
Power BI Desktop Bridge is a lightweight local server that lets external apps and agents interact directly with a running Power BI Desktop session, supporting report state checks, screenshot capture, file reloads, and faster automation via secure local APIs.
 The practical use case is AI-assisted report editing in a continuous loop — less interesting today, but worth understanding before it becomes default tooling.

- **Semantic model download behaviour changed.** 
Downloading a `.pbix` from a semantic model now gives an empty report with the dataset only; to get the report with the dataset you must go to the report in the Power BI Service. This addresses inconsistent report results from semantic model downloading.


**dbt — trust is now the dominant priority**


The 2026 State of Analytics Engineering report shows the share of respondents who say increasing trust in data and data teams rose from 66% in 2025 to 83% in 2026; the importance of speed climbed from 50% to 71%; cost reduction saw only modest movement, from 48% to 53%.
 The practical implication: governance and semantic layer investment now has explicit business backing in most organisations — use that when making the case internally.

**Snowflake — Semantic View Autopilot**

For teams on Snowflake, 
the major 2026 innovation is Semantic View Autopilot, which uses machine learning to automatically discover metric definitions from warehouse metadata and BI tool usage patterns.
 Lowers the onboarding cost for semantic layer adoption significantly — worth evaluating if Snowflake is in the stack.

sections.title: Career & Data Leadership
sections.body:
**Career & Data Leadership**

**Hiring conditions**


UK job vacancies fell again in the July–September 2026 window to around 717,000, continuing a multi-year decline
 — so the broad market is tighter than the data-specific numbers suggest. That said, 
nearly half of data roles are listed as hybrid or flexible, while 43% require on-site work
 — a useful signal that full remote is no longer the default at hiring stage.

**Team structure signals**

A fresh survey of 104 data professionals by [Integrate.io](https://www.integrate.io/blog/july-2025-trends-report-how-data-teams-are-structured/) is worth noting for anyone moving into a leadership role: 
42% of data teams report into CTO/Engineering, while only 26% report to a Head of Data; hybrid structures dominate at 42%, followed by centralised teams at 37%; and hiring capacity (32%) is the top challenge, followed by cross-team alignment (27%).
 If you're joining as Head of Data, the odds-on position is that you'll be sitting under a CTO, not a CDO — shape your pitch accordingly.

**Salary benchmark — a new data point**


The projected average salary across all UK data roles in 2026 is around £77,800, based on 2025 benchmarks plus approximately 3% annual growth.
 That's the mean across all levels; 
Edinburgh, Bristol, and Cambridge are now offering salaries at 85–92% of London equivalents while commanding only 60–70% of London's living costs — often the best total compensation-to-cost-of-living ratio in the UK for senior professionals.


**Leadership lens**


The slice of companies willing to call themselves data-driven has shrunk back to the mid-30s, down from the mid-40s two years ago, even as data and analytics spending keeps rising — "spending more, getting less," a gap that is usually a structure problem wearing a budget costume.
 The practical implication: 
in 2026, the gap between AI experimentation and AI outcomes is almost always a data strategy and governance gap
 — which makes governance ownership a concrete differentiator to signal in any senior interview.

sections.title: UK Insurance
sections.body:
**UK Insurance**

**FCA rule simplification now live**


FCA insurance rule changes came into force in June and July 2026, with the bulk taking effect on 26 June and the remainder on 27 July, per Handbook Notice No. 142.
 
The simplification programme is expected to alter claims-handling workflows, disclosure obligations and complaints processes — introducing transitional risk for firms adapting legacy systems.
 Separately, 
the FCA intends to conclude its pure protection market study later in 2026, with emphasis on closing the "protection gap" and improving claims experiences.


**Motor market**


EY's latest analysis forecasts the motor market will remain loss-making through 2026 and 2027. After a profitable 2024 (NCR 98%), the market fell back into the red in 2025 (NCR 102%), with a worse NCR of 108% forecast for 2026 — driven by premium rate reductions feeding through to earned premium alongside persistent claims inflation.
 
Defaqto expects premiums to rise in coming months, though increases are more likely to be gradual and targeted rather than the sharp spikes of the last hard-market cycle.


**Distribution: John Lewis Motor panel**


John Lewis Money's car insurance relaunch, obtaining direct FCA broker authorisation in March 2026, replaced a single-carrier appointed representative arrangement with Covéa; it now controls panel composition, product design and pricing relationships across 1.4 million existing customers.
 
The car panel launches with Ageas, AXA and Covéa.
 
The firm says 70% of existing home insurance customers have seen cheaper quotes since the April 2026 home relaunch under the same model.
 For personal lines carriers, this is a meaningful distribution shift: a high-trust retail brand with near-zero customer acquisition cost is now an active panel manager rather than a passive AR.

sections.title: Milton Keynes
sections.body:
I'll search across several angles to find what's genuinely new today.
I have one search remaining — let me use it to check for very latest MK news from this week.
**Events — diary these**

- **📅 25 Aug (Tue)** — 
NatWest Tech Tuesdays networking lunch, 11:30–13:00 at NatWest Community Hub.
 Practical format; worth bookmarking if you missed Code For Her earlier this month.

- **📅 16–18 Sep** — 
The National Museum of Computing / London Mathematical Society Conference at Bletchley Park, 10:00–17:30. Three-day event with a computing/maths crossover — niche but strong signal for the MK tech scene.


- **📅 3 Oct** — 
Festival of innovation, art, science and technology in Milton Keynes — full details still to be released.
 One to watch for more info.

- **📅 17 Sep** — 
TNMOC/London Mathematical Society Conference at Bletchley Park, 10:00–17:30.
 (Overlaps with the above; may be the same programme — check protospace.uk.)

- **📅 14 Oct** — 
MK Cyber Social Event, 18:00–21:00 at Warbler on the Wharf, Campbell Wharf Marina.
 Good pre–MK Tech Week warm-up for the security/infosec crowd.

**Local news**

- **New Towns programme.** 
In March, the Government named MK as one of seven locations under consideration for its New Towns programme. A national consultation is open — it doesn't mean approvals have been granted, but communities can submit views before final decisions.
 
The three proposed expansion areas could together deliver around 40,000 new homes, plus jobs, schools and infrastructure.


- **Marston Vale (5,000 homes).** 
MK City Council is among those commenting on outline plans for up to 5,000 homes between MK and Bedford — revised since Universal Studios was granted planning permission nearby at Marston Vale.
 Scale of neighbouring development means transport and services planning is already getting complicated.

- **Council Plan 2026/27.** 
The new Lib Dem–Labour administration has published a 70-point Council Plan, with commitments including pothole repairs, affordable homes, and new day/overnight services for adults with complex disabilities.


- **20mph consultation.** 
A new consultation proposes 20mph zone entry signs at key access points across one residential estate, with no physical traffic-calming measures planned.
 Worth watching if you're near the affected area — details on the council consultations page.
